competences: The learner describes marriage in christian life using religious education vocabulary.
The learner identifies appropriate Christian values in decisions and family relationships.
languageCompetence: Reads, spells and uses advice, peace, trust, marriage, respect, patience, tolerance, faithfulness and vows.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explain marriage in christian life.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer at least three cited exercise questions using the correct facts.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already learned the meaning of friendship and how Jesus demonstrated care, forgiveness, kindness and service to other people.
materials: P6 CRE teacher's notes on friendship and marriage
Chalkboard with source-based definitions and qualities
references: P.6 Religious Education Lesson Notes, Term III (2022)
P6 Religious Education Lesson Notes Term III

steps.teacherActivity: Begin by reviewing marriage in christian life through one familiar idea from the previous lesson. Ask learners how this week's topic builds upon respectful friendships and responsible choices.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previous work on friendship, explain their existing understanding, and respond to the opening questions.

steps.content: Meaning of marriage; Types of marriage: **Marriage** is a legal union of a man and a woman as husband and wife. The Christian lessons describe marriage as a commitment of mutual love. Marriage creates a family relationship with duties towards each partner. Holy Matrimony joins a husband and wife in the Christian community.
steps.teacherActivity: Explain meaning of marriage and types of marriage, setting out each definition and fact exactly as given in the source notes. Ask short questions to confirm understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners listen, explain the key meanings, and copy the factual chalkboard points into their notebooks.

steps.content: Qualities of a good marriage partner; Marriage vows: A faithful partner is honest and worthy of trust. A good partner shows respect, kindness and care. Patience and tolerance help partners handle everyday difficulties. Forgiveness can help married people recover from disagreements.
steps.teacherActivity: Teach qualities of a good marriage partner and marriage vows with the examples and differences provided by the source. Ask the learners to compare the ideas and identify correct choices.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify and compare source-based facts, name examples from the notes, and explain the main Christian values.

steps.content: Sourced written exercise: What is marriage? | Who presides over each of the above types of marriage? | How is Holy Matrimony important among Christians? | Why do people marry? | What is a marriage vow?
steps.teacherActivity: Give all five existing exercise questions to the class without changing their numbers or wording. Discuss answers using the original teacher notes after individual work.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the five sourced questions in writing and compare answers with the notes during correction.

steps.teacherActivity: Review the main definitions and key qualities from the chalkboard notes. Ask a final question to identify misunderstandings and assign the sourced exercise questions for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners restate what was learned, correct one answer if necessary, and note the home revision task.

assessment: Check learning from the cited source using the exact questions: What is marriage? Who presides over each of the above types of marriage? How is Holy Matrimony important among Christians? Why do people marry? What is a marriage vow? Correct individual answers in class, then give revision feedback.
homework: Answer two of the sourced questions again at home, using the teacher's facts and notes.
